title: Balanced Multimodal Federated Learning: An Efficient and Noise-Resilient Approach

problem.claim: Modality imbalance, multimodal noise, and high computational costs limit the effectiveness and deployment of multimodal federated learning.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally assume clean multimodal data, do not distinguish informative hard samples from detrimental noise, and impose prohibitive computational costs.

contributions.claim: MFedFAIR is an efficient and noise-resilient multimodal federated learning framework.
The framework introduces individual modality contribution and multimodal synergistic gain metrics to guide semantic denoising selection and robust conditional balancing.
The framework uses forward propagation to derive metrics, prioritizes informative semantically aligned samples, and supports quality-aware collaboration for robust aggregation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four benchmark datasets reportedly show that MFedFAIR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in effectiveness and efficiency in realistic noisy multimodal federated learning environments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal federated learning collaboratively trains models across modalities while preserving data privacy.
Modality imbalance prevents models from reaching the performance ceiling of joint training.
Existing methods assume clean data, mishandle modality-specific and cross-modal noise, and are computationally costly.
MFedFAIR applies utility metrics, semantic denoising, conditional balancing, forward-only metric computation, sample prioritization, and quality-aware aggregation.
The authors report superior effectiveness and efficiency across four benchmark datasets in noisy environments.

source_observation.claim: The framework quantifies sample-level and semantic-level utility to guide denoising and balancing.

interpretation.claim: Separating utility assessment from training selection may help systems handle heterogeneous or noisy multimodal data.

application.claim: This approach could inform multimodal systems that need to prioritize reliable, semantically aligned data under resource constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported federated multimodal learning settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, dataset names, baseline identities, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not specify the implementation details or overhead of the IMC and MSG metrics.
The abstract does not report privacy, communication, or reproducibility details.
